_comment: Puzzle set for the daily archive game at /guess/. Read only through
SOURCE: Wikidata, which is released under CC0. There is no attribution requirement at all, so
the licensing risk on this surface is zero. The page credits it anyway, because a publication
that prints its sources should print them when it does not have to.
Every field is a settled biographical fact rather than a statistic: nationality, the years a
player was active, the senior clubs he played for, and the shirt he is remembered in. Nothing
here needs a live feed and nothing here goes stale.
A note on shirt numbers. Fixed squad numbers only arrived in the English league in 1993 and
later still elsewhere, so for the earlier players this is the number the player is remembered
in rather than a registered squad number. The clue on the page says exactly that.
One puzzle a day, chosen from this list by date, so everyone gets the same one. Add entries to
the end: the rotation is stable as long as nothing already in the list moves.

players.name: Diego Maradona
players.note: Took a Napoli side that had never won the Italian league and won it twice.

players.name: Zinedine Zidane
players.note: Left the game with a red card in a World Cup final and a Golden Ball on the same night.

players.name: Roberto Baggio
players.note: Carried Italy to the 1994 final and then missed the penalty that lost it.

players.name: Ronaldo
players.note: Two ruptured knees between the 1998 and 2002 finals, and eight goals in the second one.

players.name: Johan Cruyff
players.note: Wore 14 because the numbers were handed out at random one afternoon, and then kept it.

players.name: Franz Beckenbauer
players.note: Won the World Cup as a captain and then again as a manager.

players.name: Eric Cantona
players.note: Left English football at thirty, at the top, and never came back to it.

players.name: Dennis Bergkamp
players.note: Refused to fly, so his club learned to travel by coach and train.

players.name: Gabriel Batistuta
players.note: Stayed with Fiorentina through relegation, which is why the city put up a statue.

players.name: Romario
players.note: Claimed a thousand career goals and then went into the Brazilian senate.

players.name: Roberto Carlos
players.note: The free kick against France in 1997 still gets argued about by physicists.

players.name: George Weah
players.note: The only African man to win the Ballon d'Or, and later president of his country.

players.name: Hristo Stoichkov
players.note: Dragged Bulgaria, who had never won a World Cup match, all the way to a semi-final.

players.name: Gheorghe Hagi
players.note: Known at home as the Maradona of the Carpathians, which he mostly earned.

players.name: Davor Suker
players.note: Won the Golden Boot at the 1998 World Cup for a country six years old.

players.name: Franco Baresi
players.note: One club, twenty seasons, and a number the club has never issued since.

players.name: Ruud Gullit
players.note: Dedicated his Ballon d'Or to Nelson Mandela, who was still in prison.

players.name: Marco van Basten
players.note: An ankle finished him at twenty-eight, four years after the volley in Munich.

players.name: Paolo Maldini
players.note: Twenty-five seasons at one club, and the shirt is held for his sons.

players.name: Michel Platini
players.note: Three Ballons d'Or in a row, from a midfielder who scored like a striker.

players.name: Lothar Matthaus
players.note: Played in five World Cups, which nobody had done before him.

players.name: Eusebio
players.note: Four goals in one game against North Korea after Portugal went three down.

players.name: Ferenc Puskas
players.note: Left Hungary after the 1956 uprising and started again in Spain at thirty-one.

players.name: Rivaldo
players.note: A hat-trick on the last day to save a Champions League place, finished with an overhead kick.

players.name: Luis Figo
players.note: Left one Spanish club for their fiercest rival and had a pig's head thrown at him for it.

players.name: Alessandro Del Piero
players.note: Stayed with Juventus through relegation to the second division and captained them back.

players.name: Bobby Charlton
players.note: Survived Munich at twenty, and lifted the European Cup ten years later.

players.name: Ryan Giggs
players.note: Scored in twenty-one consecutive Premier League seasons, which nobody else has.

players.name: Andriy Shevchenko
players.note: Took the penalty that won Milan the 2003 European Cup, and missed the one that lost 2005.

players.name: Pavel Nedved
players.note: Booked in the semi-final, so he watched the 2003 final from the stand.
